'''Andrew Harrison''' (born October 28, 1994) is an American [[basketball]] player. He was considered one of the top recruits for 2013.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/rankings/rank-2752;_ylt=Andph5Z8Rbt0UH6UB5vIFELWO5B4 Rivals.com]</ref><ref>[http://www.scout.com/a.z?s=143&p=8&c=1&nid=4763121&pg=2 Scout.com]</ref> He attended [[Travis High School (Fort Bend County, Texas)|Travis High School]] in [[Fort Bend, Texas]], and now attends [[University of Kentucky]], along with his twin brother, [[Aaron Harrison]].<ref>[http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/8462850/kentucky-wildcats-land-twin-recruits-aaron-harrison-andrew-harrison Harrison twins choose Kentucky]</ref><ref>[http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2012/10/04/2013-guards-aaron-and-andrew-harrison-verbally-commit-to-attend-kentucky/ 2013 guards Aaron and Andrew Harrison verbally commit to attend Kentucky]</ref><ref>[http://articles.centralkynews.com/2013-04-10/amnews/38442827_1_aaron-harrison-state-championship-travis-high-school Vaught's Views: Aaron Harrison shows he is a special player, like his twin brother]</ref>

Harrison played in both the [[Jordan Brand Classic#2013|2013 Jordan Brand Classic]], and the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]].<ref>[http://blogs.courier-journal.com/recruiting/2013/04/04/andrew-harrison-recaps-mcdonalds-game/ Andrew Harrison recaps McDonald’s game]</ref><ref>[http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-03-31/sports/ct-spt-0401-prep-bkb-mcdonalds-main-20130331_1_ronald-mcdonald-house-julius-randle-andrew-harrison Kentucky recruits dominate McDonald's All-American game rosters]</ref>

==High School Career==
[[File:20130403 MCDAAG Andrew Harrison drives on Kasey Hill.JPG|left|thumb|upright|Harrison driving on Kasey Hill during the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]]
Andrew Harrison was widely regarded as a top 5 player in the class of 2013 with [[Andrew Wiggins]], [[Jabari Parker]], [[Julius Randle]], and twin brother [[Aaron Harrison]].
On March 9, Andrew Harrison along with his twin brother [[Aaron Harrison]] helped the Fort Bend Travis Tigers (In Sugarland,TX) to defeat South Grand Prairie, 46-38 at The University of Texas at Austin to win the Class 5A state title in Texas. They finished #16 in the final ESPN 25 Power Rankings. Fort Bend Travis had lost in the Class 5A state title game the year before to Flower Mound Marcus. He now plays alongside his brother as sophomores at Kentucky.<ref>[http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/powerrankings?week=99&season=2012/fort-bend-travis-tigers-wins-class-5A-state-title/ Fort Bend Travis Tigers wins Class 5A state title]</ref><ref>[http://espn.go.com/blog/high-school/texas/tag/_/name/fort-bend-travis/fort-bend-travis-tigers-defeated-by-flower-mound-marcus-the-year-before/ Fort Bend Travis Tigers defeated by Flower Mound Marcus the year before]</ref>

==College career==
On April 9, 2015 Harrison along with his Kentucky teammates [[Aaron Harrison]], [[Dakari Johnson]], [[Devin Booker]], [[Trey Lyles]], [[Karl-Anthony Towns]] and [[Willie Cauley-Stein]] declared to enter their names into the [[2015 NBA Draft]].
